rejected.title: The strategic role of marketing
card: Marketing is the link between a business and its customers. It finds out what customers want and passes this on to the rest of the business.
A strategic role means marketing helps shape where the whole business is heading. Its decisions affect what the business makes, how it prices and where it sells.
Marketing helps a business win new customers and keep existing ones. Customers who return often give steady sales.
Sales are the amount sold. Market share is the business's portion of total sales in its market. Profit is what is left after costs are paid. Good marketing can build all three.
rejected.remember: Marketing connects the business to its customers to win and keep them, which can build sales, market share and profit.

a.q: Which describes the strategic role of marketing in a business?
opts: It links the business to customers to win and keep them
It makes the goods that the business sells
It sets the wages paid to the staff of the business
It records the money coming in and going out each week
a.why: Marketing connects the business to its customers and helps it win and keep them. Making goods is operations, not marketing, which is the most tempting wrong option because marketing does shape what is made.
a.clue: Think about who marketing connects the business with.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange adds a gluten-free range after surveys show many local customers ask for it. Sales rise and more customers return each week. What does this best show?
opts: Marketing used customer information to win and keep buyers
Marketing worked only because the bakery advertised more
Marketing raised the bakery's share by cutting its costs
Marketing stayed separate from what the bakery produced
b.why: The bakery found out what customers wanted and changed what it sold, which won and kept customers. The advertising option is tempting but wrong, because nothing in the case mentions advertising and marketing is more than that.
b.clue: Look at what the bakery did after the surveys.

opts: It links the business to customers to help win and keep them
It runs the daily production of the goods the business sells

It records the money the business earns and spends each year
a.why: Marketing connects the business to its customers and helps it win and keep them. Running production is the tempting wrong option: what marketing learns can shape what the business makes, but marketing does not run the making of the goods.

b.q: Priya's bakery in Orange surveys locals and finds many want gluten-free bread. She adds it to her range. Sales and repeat customers rise. What does this best show?
opts: Marketing findings guided what the business decided to sell
Marketing's role here was to advertise bread already made
Production chose the new bread, then marketing promoted it
Sales rose because the bakery lowered its bread prices
b.why: The survey found what customers wanted, and that shaped what the bakery sold, which won and kept customers. The advertising option is tempting, but the bakery did not just promote existing bread: marketing's findings changed what was made.
b.clue: Look at what led Priya to add the new bread.
